note: Thresholds from pack-distinct-calibration.spec.ts. Each score has an alike line (null when its calibration found no gap of 0.1 at both viewports, so it doesn't vote) and a clone floor. A pair fails when its pixels are under their alike line, whatever its tokens say (the token line decides only while the pixels have none), or when either score is under its clone floor. For a design language the token score reads only the groups a static render shows (corners, depth, borders, density), and the material (surface) only when the composition's render shows a visible Surface primitive (`material` records that detection and its reason); focus, motion, states, icons, texture, and an unrendered material are informational lines that never score. `pinned` true holds `composition` as the scored one whatever the coverage procedure picks, and `procedurePick` records that pick and its coverage. `enforced` false reports failures without failing the run. `rulings` names pairs that pass while failing, each with why; a `scope` (a viewport, desktop or mobile) holds a ruling to those rows only, so the pair still fails anywhere else, and `evidence` names the shots that carry it.

material.reason: visible Surfaces cover 0 at desktop and 0 at mobile, under 0.02 of the first viewport at one or more viewport: the material is informational

rulings.ruling: SB at 390 reads box height, and these share one; ruled at 390 only; apart at 1440 since fluent-2-inspired 1.1.5 (0.144) (lead A, 2026-10-31; LANG-5c decision 1a, r2)
rulings.why: Spatial Bento paints canvas tiles from the language's shape, elevation, border and control-height tokens and no Surface, so a language's tonal colour, texture and stylesheet never reach its tiles. At 390, where its tiles stack, the edges mostly measure control height and border width, and Fluent and Primer both keep their real 32px controls (2rem). At 1440 Fluent's elevation ramp (cards at shadow28, a 36% key) lifts every tile where Primer draws a hairline: 0.087 before r2, 0.144 now, over the 0.113 line, so the pair is ruled at 390 only. The lift barely shows in dark (the shadow role is black), which the strips record.

rulings.ruling: ALIKE on SB at both viewports: SB's canvas tiles don't paint M3's signature, tonal colour and filled controls; ruled on SB (lead A, 2026-10-31; LANG-5c r2, option a)
rulings.why: Spatial Bento paints canvas tiles from the language's shape, elevation, border and control-height tokens and no Surface, so a language's tonal colour, texture and stylesheet never reach its tiles. Material 3 and platform-neutral share what SB does paint: rounded tiles, a two-layer card elevation, 40px pill controls. By eye they read ALIKE on SB at 1440 and 390, in light and dark (B's strip review), and the pixels agree (0.087 at 1440, 0.173 at 390). M3's signature is the tonal colour and the filled controls, which show where the primitives paint: Editorial Evidence's Actions and Fields, and Studio. No honest M3 token SB paints separates them (probe 3: level-1, level-2 and level-3 card elevations score 0.087 to 0.092). Painting tile material on SB, with the 528-pair recalibration, is post-surge (a known gap the lead holds with the owner). platform-neutral is the anchor and doesn't move.
evidence: _execution/artifacts/kgn-b-languages/lang5c/r2-strips-af02cb2b8/signatures.png (actions and field rows: M3's filled tonal button and filled field against platform-neutral's)

rulings.ruling: apart at 1440 (0.172); at 390 SB's score reads stacked control height and frame thickness, and by eye the frames read clearly apart (strips at aea99e449); ruled at 390 only (lead A, 2026-10-31; LANG-5c r1, option 1)
rulings.why: Spatial Bento paints canvas tiles from the language's tokens and no Surface, so at 390, where its tiles stack, its edges mostly measure control height and frame thickness. pixel-interface's controls are 2.25rem and its frame 6px (a 2px ring outside a 4px border); the stacks nearly coincide, they don't share a height. At 1440 the pair clears the line at 0.172; at 390 it scores 0.199. By eye, on every tile in light and dark: pixel-interface's hard 6px square ink frame against synthwave's 2px rust line with a soft halo that bleeds into the gutter; synthwave's accent on every frame edge, pixel-interface's inside the content. pixel-interface 1.0.5's 390 frames now separate (5 CSS px of page ground in every SB gutter), so these tiles are the shipped look (strip review, option 1). Editorial Evidence, report only, reads the pair apart at both viewports.
